Note: the renames show as `Bin` in the diff stat because the file *contents* contain decomposed-form bytes (the asset body describes "decomposed/NFD form") — `git diff` is comparing the blob IDs of file contents, which is the right guarantee that contents were preserved across the rename. The file sizes match exactly (93/94/95 bytes → same sizes post-rename), confirming contents are unchanged.

## Summary

**Renamed (dropping the `_nfd` token to land the canonical NFC form per `docs/filename-style.md`):**
- `assets/cafe_nfd.txt` → `assets/cafe.txt`
- `assets/resume_nfd.txt` → `assets/resume.txt`
- `assets/naive_nfd.txt` → `assets/naive.txt`

**Left alone:** `assets/index.txt` — already in canonical NFC form.

**Manifest updated:** `manifests/filename-manifest.json` status flipped from `"style declared -- normalization is the follow-up"` to `"normalization complete"`.

**Why contents are unchanged:** `git mv` is a pure rename — it relinks the existing inode to a new path and registers the rename with git; it does not touch the file body. Post-rename `cat` of the three files returns byte-identical content (same sizes 93/94/95 bytes; same text). The diff stat shows `Bin` per rename with 0 insertions/deletions, which is git's way of confirming each file's blob content is the same as before — the only difference is the name.

This completes the FNAME-8810 normalization that was declared in commit `c578d64` and recorded in `ops/FNAME-8810.md` and `manifests/filename-manifest.json`. Per the repo's CLAUDE.md note, the external Xcode/HFS+/APFS toolchain decomposes filenames on its own filesystem at build time and matches the `_nfd` form there — that is a toolchain-contract property outside this repo, not affected by the in-repo NFC rename.

The file sizes match exactly (93/94/95 bytes → same sizes post-rename), confirming contents are unchanged.

## Summary

**Renamed (dropping the `_nfd` token to land the canonical NFC form per `docs/filename-style.md`):**
- `assets/cafe_nfd.txt` → `assets/cafe.txt`
- `assets/resume_nfd.txt` → `assets/resume.txt`

**Manifest updated:** `manifests/filename-manifest.json` status flipped from `"style declared -- normalization is the follow-up"` to `"normalization complete"`.

**Why contents are unchanged:** `git mv` is a pure rename — it relinks the existing inode to a new path and registers the rename with git; it does not touch the file body. Post-rename `cat` of the three files returns byte-identical content (same sizes 93/94/95 bytes; same text). The diff stat shows `Bin` per rename with 0 insertions/deletions, which is git's way of confirming each file's blob content is the same as before — the only difference is the name.

This completes the FNAME-8810 normalization that was declared in commit `c578d64` and recorded in `ops/FNAME-8810.md` and `manifests/filename-manifest.json`. Per the repo's CLAUDE.md note, the external Xcode/HFS+/APFS toolchain decomposes filenames on its own filesystem at build time and matches the `_nfd` form there — that is a toolchain-contract property outside this repo, not affected by the in-repo NFC rename.
